sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year, from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F201][F1][F10].
The path was uneven: revenue fell 22.4% in FY2020 [D198], then rose 22.1% in FY2021 [D251] and 16.6% in FY2022 [D304].
The FY2020 drop reflected lower end-user demand and dealer inventory changes across the three primary segments [P59]; operating margin fell 4.5pp to 10.9% [D211][F25].
The FY2023 margin gain of 6.0pp to 19.3% [D370][F28] reflected price realization, higher volume and the absence of the FY2022 Rail goodwill impairment of $925 million [P31][X117].
Power Energy was the largest FY2025 contributor, adding 5.2pp to revenue growth of 4.3% [D759][D463] and reaching 47.6% of revenue [D757].
Its Power Generation unit grew 32.5% [D894], adding 3.9pp [D895]; the cited passages give no cause for that move.
Construction Industries fell 1.6% [D765] because unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion outweighed $568 million of added volume [P8].
Operating costs rose 9.1% [D481] against revenue growth of 4.3% [D463], so operating income fell 14.7% [D464], an incremental margin of -69.1% [D488].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% [D467], less than the 17.7% net income drop [D465], as the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Growth rests on one segment whose FY2025 driver the filings leave unexplained.
Operating margin of 16.5% [F30] sits above its 14.3% window median [D1123] and below the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1122].

The 3.7pp fall [D476] came mostly from cost of revenue, which cost 4.2pp [D490] as its share rose to 66.2% from 62.0% [D441][D388]; the filing blames $2.148 billion of unfavorable manufacturing costs, largely tariffs [P9].
Cost of revenue supplied 5.8pp of the FY2023 gain of 6.0pp [D384][D370], second only to FY2017's 6.8pp [D52].
The effective tax rate rose to 24.0% [D449] from 19.7% [D396], a move the cited filings do not explain, pushing net margin of 13.1% [F50] further below operating margin of 16.5% [F30].
Free cash flow of $8.92 billion [F100] equalled 1.00x net income [D451], against a 0.96x window median [D1135], after an 11.2% fall [D469].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose on lower working capital and cash taxes [P4], yet consolidated operating cash flow fell 2.5% to $11.7 billion [D468][F80].
Capital expenditure rose 41.9% to $2.82 billion [D470][F90], and the filing cites higher capital expenditure in investing outflows [P3]; capex is now 1.25x depreciation and amortization [D452].
Net cash of -$26.2 billion [D456] was -38.8% of revenue [D457], the 43rd percentile of seven industrials peers, whose median is -35.6% [D1151][D1152].

Financial Products' $2.71 billion financing inflow came from higher borrowings, including intercompany loans from Machinery, Power & Energy [P2], and long-term debt rose 12.2% to $30.7 billion [D474][F190].
The current ratio of 1.44x [F180] is just above its 1.40x window median [D1138], and cash rose 44.9% to $9.98 billion [D472][F140].
Buybacks of $5.19 billion [X140] and dividends of $2.75 billion [X150] absorbed 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], while diluted shares fell 3.5% [D483].
R1 overstates the signal: net cash has been negative every year since FY2016 [D14], so the real issue is the widening from -$22.1 billion [D350] to -$26.2 billion [D456] [R1].
Operating income fell 14.7% to $11.2 billion [D464][F20], the first fall since FY2020 [D199], which the filing blames on $2.148 billion of manufacturing costs, largely tariffs [P9].
Volume was positive, so the drop is a cost and price issue rather than a demand one, and persistence hinges on pricing and cost recovery [P9].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 is proxy-sourced and can differ from the 10-K by up to 0.06% [R3]; the FY2025 gap is $2 million [F40][X20], which changes no conclusion.
Operating margin staying above its 14.3% median [D1123] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm FY2025 as a one-year dip; a fall below it would point to a lasting squeeze.
Net cash below -$26.2 billion [D456] in the FY2026 10-K would extend the widening; a return above -$24.9 billion [D403] would reverse it.
Cost of revenue below 66.2% of revenue [D441] in the FY2026 10-K would show the squeeze easing, though the first-quarter outlook still expects higher manufacturing costs in three segments [P14].
